radiology_report:
Amsterdam UMC (location AMC) | 15 January 2025 | Multiparametric MRI Prostate

Clinical Indication:
Re-evaluation for rising PSA (10.92 ng/mL) and prior positive biopsy. Clinical suspicion for clinically significant prostate cancer.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume measures 42.0 mL. A focal lesion is identified in the left peripheral zone, extending from the base to the mid gland, measuring approximately 18 × 14 × 12 mm. The lesion demonstrates marked hypointensity on T2-weighted images, restricted diffusion on DWI with corresponding low ADC values, and early focal enhancement on dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences. No extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy or osseous lesions are seen.

IMPRESSION:
- PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone.
- Prostate volume 42.0 mL; PSA density 0.26 ng/mL/mL.
- csPCa predicted probability 0.8727174.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical review addressed a fluctuating PSA trajectory, recording 9.3 ng/mL in March followed by 8.6 ng/mL in July 2024. Earlier tissue sampling established Gleason 4+3 disease. Hypertension remains well-managed through valsartan and lisinopril therapy.
